Repair only joint_test profiling/certification, numerical range handling, focused regressions and directly generated result/table/interpretation/figures/manifests. The two new counterexamples are different failure regimes of repair_01: (i) a narrow direct ball gives small objective curvature and the max(1, ...) stationarity floor falsely certifies a nonminimum, and (ii) unequal ball radii let normalized optimizer feasibility tolerances and the 1+1e-8 reconstruction check enlarge Dmax, giving a false compatible verdict. A small absolute gradient, solver success or raw KKT residual is never a membership certificate.

Separate optimization from the final scientific decision. Solve the three-variable convex profile using stable centered/scaled residuals or the quadratic H=A^T A, g=A^T b after removing any constant perpendicular term. Normalize the varying quadratic by its own nonzero curvature/linear scale, not an arbitrary 1 floor, a large canceled signal or B; retain exact-zero branches and use the well-conditioned nonzero STF lift without a new absolute S threshold. A stable unconstrained least-squares/inverse candidate may be used first when its feasibility is independently established. Keep analytic derivatives and bounded iteration, and expose typed NUMERICAL_FAILURE/NUMERIC_RANGE if an operation or convergence cannot be certified.

For every true compatibility verdict, verify a primal witness lies in the original closed direct and physical balls and its full seven-component residual is within the unchanged B, permitting only the already justified signal-relative cancellation roundoff allowance. Optimizer constraint tolerances must not become radius inflation. Repair/projection of a witness is allowed only if both original constraints are rechecked and the residual is recomputed at that feasible witness; near-boundary uncertainty must trigger higher-precision/outward arithmetic or a typed unresolved outcome. Preserve exact e_d=0, Dmax=0, empty/tangent intersections and S=0 set cases.

For a false compatibility verdict with a nonempty feasible set, require a valid lower bound on the true minimum residual above B after numerical-error accounting. An approximate KKT point alone is insufficient. A suitable finite certificate is a convex dual/primal gap or a support-function lower bound. For normalized f(d)=0.5||r(d)||^2 and gradient g at a feasible d*, convexity gives lower bounds f(d*)+g·(d_obs-d*)-e_d||g|| and, if Dmax exists, f(d*)-g·d*-Dmax||g||; their maximum with zero is valid. A nonnegative-multiplier quadratic Lagrangian dual, evaluated by a stable small linear solve, can give a sharper bound. Derive whichever bound is implemented and conservatively account for all rounding in residual, gradient, support, solve and bound conversion. Use scaled norms/bounds to avoid underflow/overflow when comparing to B. If the lower and upper bounds straddle the decision boundary, return typed numerical unresolved rather than a scientific rejection. Existing cancellation allowance may account only for representational signal cancellation; it must not hide optimization error or a witness outside either physical ball. A scalar profile score may be labelled the optimum only when its bound/gap supports that accuracy; otherwise label an upper bound/interval or return unresolved. Do not silently overclaim a globally exact profile.

Guard all returned numerical fields: the finite O=(1e200,0,...), S=0, d_obs=0, B=0 control must not return Inf in residual_squared/perpendicular_squared. Return an explicit typed NUMERIC_RANGE for an unrepresentable requested quantity (or finite residual plus explicitly typed unavailable display metadata if supported consistently); never rely on a later JSON serialization failure. Preserve robust norms, nonzero S at 1e-200, and unrepresentable response handling.

Add exact frozen new false-rejection and false-acceptance inputs from this REVIEW_RESULT.counterexample, plus their rotations/common output-unit rescalings and the residual-display range control. Include an analytic one-axis interval oracle across narrow e_d/d_obs and large e_d/Dmax ratios, checking strict original-ball feasibility and residual decision bounds. Retain the three old counterexamples, 0.8/0.8 joint rejection, correlated covariance, STF/frame/c/units, rank/support, boost chart/shifted vertex and source finite-z controls. Run only this focused suite and consumer, with outputs in the new candidate and raw failures preserved; no broad historical reruns. The recorded easy feasible witness must return compatible with a valid witness; the recorded infeasible-budget case must return incompatible with a valid lower bound or explicit numerical unresolved, never compatible. Send the exact next manifest and raw logs to this nonauthor reviewer for one targeted closeout; acceptance and qualification remain false pending that independent decision. No automatic ultra escalation or renamed exhausted attempt is authorized.

Preferred numerical certificate refinement: use the nonsquared norm-objective lower bound validated in /mnt/extdrive/workdir/htt_open_data/r36_optical_repair_independent_review/NORM_BOUND_CONTRACT.json (sha256:85b268eb8e03172364b48501362fb6abad0eade98c9a7a7e055daa224e8a295d). For phi(d)=||O-A d||, q=-A^T r/||r|| (valid zero-residual subgradient at r=0), g1=||d-d_obs||-e_d, optional g2=||d||-Dmax, norm-constraint subgradients n_i and arbitrary finite lambda_i>=0, min_C phi >= phi(d)+sum lambda_i*g_i(d)-||q+sum lambda_i*n_i||*D, where D is an upper bound from the minimum of the applicable ball triangle bounds. This follows from convex supporting inequalities plus Cauchy, with no KKT convergence assumption. Use valid zero-center subgradients; conservatively enclose every quantity and accumulated arithmetic error, round D upward and the final certificate downward, and apply only the original justified signal-cancellation error policy. A verified primal upper bound decides true, a conservative lower bound above B decides false, and an undecided interval yields typed numerical unresolved. Strict original-ball feasibility is independent of normalized optimizer tolerances.
